description: Family 12 (docs/tasks.md section 15): a watcher guards a vault split into fixed-size BitVM3 claim graphs, each paying a derived key P' six blocks after its claim unless someone spends the claim output with the reject label of the garbled M14 verifier. Claims arrive over a horizon; some are fraudulent. The watcher has one machine, a cheap native check that catches one fraud class, and the fee market to beat the window in. The graph, its timelocks, sizes and presigned fee are the In-and-Out-Burger graph's; the evaluation latency is measured; every other number is a bench decision unless provenance says otherwise.

provenance.graph: given: Spiral main ad235c4, in-and-out-burger/iob/bitvm3.py (last changed in 76071a0): vault V = NUMS + {claim: <D> CHECKSIGVERIFY <C> CHECKSIG, reclaim: <144> CSV DROP <D> CHECKSIG}; claim K = NUMS + {payout: <6> CSV DROP <D> CHECKSIG -> P', disprove: SHA256 <H(reject)> EQUALVERIFY <W> CHECKSIG} + OP_RETURN IOB3 || claim_id. One graph per claim, so a vault is a set of fixed-size UTXOs (in-and-out-burger/README.md, last changed in 03be853)
provenance.window_blocks: given: WINDOW_BLOCKS = 6 in iob/bitvm3.py; Bitcoin Core 31.1 refused the payout at 3 and 5 confirmations as non-BIP68-final and accepted it at 6 (in-and-out-burger/results/bitvm3-regtest.json)
provenance.reclaim_blocks: given: RECLAIM_BLOCKS = 144 in iob/bitvm3.py. Every claim here arrives within 24 blocks of the vault, so the reclaim never preempts a claim
provenance.presigned_fee_sat_vb: given: FEE_SAT_VB = 2 in iob/bitvm3.py; the claim and the payout are presigned at it
provenance.vbytes: given: measured on testnet4, in-and-out-burger/results/testnet4-bitvm3/summary.json (last changed in 33ec5db): claim 208 vB (fee 416 sats at 2 sat/vB, as in graph-honest.json), payout 128 vB, disprove 138 vB
provenance.dust_sats: given: iob/bitvm3.py refuses a graph whose payout or disprove output is not above 330 sats
provenance.vault_sats: invented: four fixed UTXO sizes, drawn uniformly, from 100,000 to 1,000,000 sats. The M16 mainnet payment the desk replayed earns a 948,400-sat payout, inside the range (in-and-out-burger/README.md); the testnet4 demonstration's 25,000 and 10,000-sat vaults (results/testnet4-bitvm3/graph-*.json) were test amounts. A wider menu, 10,000 to 2,000,000, left two cells without measurable headroom on eight seeds
provenance.classes: invented shares, in parts per million. The two fraud classes are the testnet4 demonstration's two dishonest instances (README, Testnet4 BitVM3 bonded payout): wrong_statement hands over a valid proof of another statement, which the native verifier refuses (statement_digest_mismatch in the desk's proven replay); invalid_proof hands over a proof that verifies natively but input labels that encode a different one (tampered-proof flips input bit 8,635,040, results/testnet4-bitvm3/m14-eval-tampered-proof.json), which only the garbled evaluation sees. The share is high because a false claim costs the claimant nothing (BitVMArena corpus/docs/BITVM3.md at 57a038d, finding 4)
provenance.check: given: the native final verifier checks the 1,099,069-byte proof in 0.012 s on one thread (garbled-snark-verifier nova-bitvm3/m13/README.md, last changed in 03c56e6; 0.011 s in results/testnet4-bitvm3/native-verify.json); the bench charges it nothing but a step
provenance.eval_blocks: invented within a measured range: m14-claim evaluate on the 785,442,492-gate, 8,635,080-input-bit M14 circuit took 237-279 s on a 16 GB hosted runner and 627-1,330 s on the laptop while swapping (BitVMArena corpus/docs/BITVM3.md at 57a038d), 348-401 s on the laptop in the testnet4 run (results/testnet4-bitvm3/m14-eval-*.json), and 3,607 s at 17.6 GB peak in a selftest under load (in-and-out-burger/results/m14-claim-selftest.json, last changed in d48f42d): 0.4 to 6.0 blocks of 600 s. The bench takes the slowest swapping run, 1,330 s, in whole blocks: 3. An evaluation started in the block a claim confirms then leaves two blocks to confirm its disprove, and one started a block later leaves one
provenance.eval_cost_sats: invented: what one evaluation costs the watcher in machine time and power
provenance.fees: family 11's fee model (config/swap.json, docs/tasks.md section 14.1), unchanged: a log-uniform base of 2 to 40 sat/vB and a lognormal walk per block
provenance.cells: invented: watch has no spike and no reorganization. fee_spike has two spike slots, each with probability 0.8 a spike of family 11's shape (4x to 15x for 3 to 8 blocks), starting 1 to 4 blocks after a burst of claims, so it can cover that burst's disprove window. reorg replaces a burst's block, with probability 0.5, by blocks without it, and the claims confirm again 1 or 2 blocks later, restarting their windows; testnet4 did this to a claim, mined in 161,710 and again in 161,712 (BitVMArena corpus/docs/TESTNET4.md at 57a038d)
provenance.arrivals: invented: 4 to 6 bursts of 1 to 3 claims at distinct heights in the 24 blocks after the start, so 4 to 18 claims an episode
provenance.budget: invented: generous enough to act on every claim at every block
